inputs_used: Smartraveller Pacific pages for Fiji, Vanuatu, New Caledonia, French Polynesia, Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga (live 26 Nov 2026)

facts.claim: [Copied from wedding-destinations-november 03-source-pack fact fact_108, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller Fiji (updated 19 October 2026, still current at 24 November 2026, read live 25 November 2026): 'November to April is cyclone season, but cyclones may occur at other times.' A tropical cyclone's direction and strength can change quickly; during and after a cyclone flights to and from affected areas can be delayed or suspended and available flights may fill quickly. For cyclone updates check the Fiji Meteorological Service.

[Copied from wedding-destinations-november 03-source-pack fact fact_109, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller Fiji (updated 19 October 2026, read live 25 November 2026): 'Flooding is common, especially in downtown Nadi and on the Coral Coast.' Floods can cut off road access, including access to the airport; monitor road closures on the Fiji Roads Authority Facebook page.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Fiji (re-read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 25 November 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'; overall 'Exercise normal safety precautions'). The cyclone line is unchanged: 'November to April is cyclone season, but cyclones may occur at other times.' Latest update: 'Fiji has declared a National State of Disaster due to worsening El Niño conditions. Water supplies may be impacted, and water rationing may be in place.' 'Monitor weather conditions before you travel. Check with your travel provider or hotel for updates.'
facts.conflicts: fact_101 records the page as 'updated 19 October 2026' (read 25 November 2026); the live page now shows 'Updated: 25 November 2026'. Cyclone wording is the same; use the 25 November 2026 update date.

facts.claim: As at November 2026, Smartraveller Fiji, Local laws (read live 26 November 2026): 'Outside of tourist areas, dress standards are conservative. Take care not to offend.' No line on getting married appears in the overview.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Vanuatu (read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 09 November 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'; overall 'Exercise normal safety precautions'): 'The cyclone season is from November to April, but cyclones and tropical storms can sometimes occur outside this.' 'The direction and strength of a tropical cyclone can change suddenly.' If a cyclone or tropical storm occurs, 'flights could be delayed or suspended', 'available flights may fill quickly' and 'the storm may affect access to seaports'. It points to the National Disaster Management Office and the Vanuatu Meteorological and Geo-Hazards Department.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Vanuatu latest update (read live 26 November 2026): 'Effective from 5 November, local authorities have prohibited aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats from operating at Santo International Airport until the airport's rescue and firefighting services are fully operational. Reconfirm your flight with your travel agent or airline.'

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Vanuatu, Local laws (read live 26 November 2026): 'It's illegal for supermarkets to sell alcohol between midday Saturday and 7am Monday. You can still buy alcohol in hotels, bars and clubs.' 'Vanuatu is a religious country (predominantly Christian) and standards of dress and behaviour are modest. Take care not to offend.' No line on getting married appears in the overview.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller New Caledonia (read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 27 August 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'). Overall: 'Exercise a high degree of caution'. 'We advise: Exercise a high degree of caution in New Caledonia due to the risk of civil disorder and violence.' Latest update: 'There's a high police and security presence in New Caledonia. Isolated security incidents may occur across the territory. Monitor local media and follow the advice of local authorities.' Quote exactly; no softening.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller New Caledonia (read live 26 November 2026): 'Authorities may impose restrictions, including curfews and bans on alcohol sales, at short notice. Essential services may be affected.' 'International and domestic flights may be suspended with little or no warning.' Demonstrations may increase around '13 May (anniversary of the 2024 civil unrest)', '24 September, (New Caledonia Citizenship Day)' and 'Election periods'.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller New Caledonia (read live 26 November 2026): 'Cyclone season is from November to May, but cyclones and severe weather can occur at any time. They can cause landslides and flooding and may disrupt essential services.' Full advice: 'Cyclone season is from November to May, but cyclones and severe weather can occur at other times.' New Caledonia has a 4-phase cyclone alert system (pre-alert, alert 1, alert 2, safeguard phase).
facts.conflicts: New Caledonia's season runs to May on Smartraveller, one month longer than the November to April stated for Fiji, Vanuatu, French Polynesia, the Cook Islands, Samoa and Tonga. Do not group it with 'November to April'.

facts.claim: As at November 2026, Smartraveller New Caledonia, Local laws and Travel (read live 26 November 2026): 'New Caledonia is an overseas territory of France. A mix of French and local laws apply. You must always have photo identification with you.' 'Outside of tourist areas, standards of dress and behaviour are conservative.' 'You need permission from customary authorities to visit certain areas.' 'Travel insurance is mandatory for entry to New Caledonia.'

As at November 2026, Smartraveller French Polynesia (read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 22 July 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'; overall 'Exercise normal safety precautions'): 'The cyclone season is between November and April. However, tropical storms and cyclones are likely to occur at any time.' Full advice: 'Cyclone season is from November to April. However, tropical storms and cyclones occur at any time of year.' 'The direction and strength of tropical cyclones can change with little warning'; flights could be delayed or suspended and ports may close. French Polynesia has a cyclone alert system with 6 levels.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller French Polynesia (read live 26 November 2026): 'French Polynesia is an overseas territory of France. A mix of French and local laws apply.' 'By law, you must always have photo identification with you.' 'Outside of tourist areas, standards of dress and behaviour are conservative.' 'Australia has a Consulate-General in Papeete, on the island of Tahiti. They can provide consular assistance and passport services. They can't notarise documents.' 'No beaches in French Polynesia are patrolled.'

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Cook Islands (read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 11 November 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'; overall 'Exercise normal safety precautions'): 'Cyclone season is from November to April, but severe storms can happen anytime. Know your accommodation's evacuation plan and your nearest shelter.' Full advice: 'Tropical storms and cyclones can happen in any month'; flights could be delayed or suspended and ports may close. 'Authorities will issue you a visa on arrival, generally a 90-day visitor visa.'

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Cook Islands (read live 26 November 2026): 'The Cook Islands' standards of dress and behaviour are modest. Be careful not to offend, especially outside resort areas.' 'There are no lifeguards on beaches.' No line on getting married appears in the overview.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Samoa (read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 05 August 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'; overall 'Exercise normal safety precautions'): 'Cyclone season is November to April, but storms occur year-round. They can cause flooding and disrupt services.' Full advice: 'Cyclone season is from November to April. However, tropical storms and cyclones can happen any time of year.' 'Roads can be cut off. It may take time for services, such as electricity, to be restored.' Latest update: 'There's an ongoing dengue outbreak in Samoa since 2025.'

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Samoa, Local laws (read live 26 November 2026): 'The legal drinking age is 21.' 'Samoa has conservative dress and behaviour standards. Take care not to offend.' 'Sunday activities are extremely limited, particularly in rural areas. Alcohol can't be sold in supermarkets. Be respectful when passing through villages on a Sunday.'

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Tonga (read live 26 November 2026; 'Updated: 11 September 2026', 'Still current at: 26 November 2026'; overall 'Exercise normal safety precautions'): 'Between November and April, Tonga is prone to cyclones, but severe storms and flash flooding can happen year-round.' Full advice: 'The cyclone season is usually from November to April. However, tropical storms and cyclones can happen throughout the year.' 'Due to El Niño conditions, the Tonga Meteorological Service has forecast a higher-than-average number of tropical cyclones this coming season, some of which may be severe.' Latest update: drought declared in Ha'apai, 'Eua and Tongatapu; 'At this time, it's not impacting tourism services'.

As at November 2026, Smartraveller Tonga, Local laws and Travel (read live 26 November 2026): 'Sabbath laws strictly limit Sunday activities including working (unless exempt), playing sport, listening to loud music and fishing.' 'Most businesses are closed except for some resorts and restaurants. Tours, including whale tours, and airports don't operate on a Sunday.' 'Tonga is a conservative country. Dress modestly'. 'Inter-island ferry schedules are typically posted only one week before.'

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_41, same source and date.] Smartraveller (last updated Tuesday 18/08/2026): 'You can't register an overseas marriage in Australia. But in most cases, your marriage is legally recognised here. To be recognised, when you got married it must have been: valid under the law of the country where it happened; valid under Australian law if it had occurred in Australia.'

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_42, same source and date.] Smartraveller: 'A foreign marriage certificate is usually accepted as proof of the marriage. But you may be unable to use it as proof of a name change. Find out from your local registry of births, deaths and marriages.'

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_43, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (last updated 18/08/2026, read live 12 November 2026): some countries ask you to prove you aren't already married; the most common documents are a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) and certificates from a registry of births, deaths and marriages; the country may have more rules (for example a residence period); 'We can't tell you what you will need'; contact your destination's embassy or consulate.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_45, same source and date.] As at November 2026, Smartraveller (read live 11 November 2026) says DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities only accept CNIs issued in their country, so ask the destination's embassy or consulate whether you need a CNI, whether you can get it in Australia, and whether it also needs an authentication or apostille.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_06, same source and date.] As at November 2026, AGD 'Get married' (re-read live 26 November 2026), 'Get married overseas': 'Overseas marriages cannot be: performed by an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant; registered in Australia.' 'An overseas marriage is generally recognised in Australia if it: was a valid marriage in the overseas country; would have been a valid marriage here.' 'You may be able to use your overseas marriage certificate to prove that you got married. However, some states and territories don't accept overseas marriage certificates if you want to change your name.' Smartraveller has information on getting married overseas.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_24, same source and date.] Before getting married you must apply for a marriage licence, which confirms it is legal for you to marry; a fee applies.
[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_25, same source and date.] You do not need to be a New Zealand citizen; visitors to New Zealand can marry in New Zealand.
[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_26, same source and date.] You need to arrange the licence at least 3 working days before you marry, and it expires after 3 months.
[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_27, same source and date.] Anyone can apply for a marriage licence online, whether in New Zealand or not; a paper form is also available.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_29, same source and date.] When couples from outside New Zealand arrive in New Zealand, they need to visit a registry office to sign a declaration before the ceremony; addresses are on the application form.
[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_32, same source and date.] You can only have the ceremony in the places you put on the licence application, so include a back-up venue.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_33, same source and date.] As at November 2026, the Hawaii State Department of Health Vital Records page "Marriage and Civil Union Licenses" (read live 16 November 2026): to lawfully marry in the State of Hawaii, a licence must be obtained from an authorised agent (Section 572-1.7, Hawaii Revised Statutes). A marriage licence (which permits the marriage) and a marriage certificate (which shows a legal marriage has been performed) are different documents.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_35, same source and date.] As at November 2026, the Hawaii State Department of Health Vital Records page "Marriage and Civil Union Licenses" (read live 16 November 2026): step 2 is to meet with an agent no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony date; the agent reviews the application, verifies photo IDs and any necessary documentation, and issues the licence. Applicants must appear together in person before an agent; proxies are not allowed.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_37, same source and date.] As at November 2026, the Hawaii State Department of Health Vital Records page "Marriage and Civil Union Licenses" (read live 16 November 2026): the official ceremony must take place within 30 days of picking up the licence; there is no waiting period before the ceremony; the licence is only valid within the State of Hawaii; if the ceremony is not performed within the 30-day period the licence is null and void.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_38, same source and date.] As at November 2026, the Hawaii State Department of Health Vital Records page "Marriage and Civil Union Licenses" (read live 16 November 2026): there are no state residence or U.S. citizenship requirements, and blood tests are not required.

[Copied from marriage-licence 03-source-pack fact fact_40, same source and date.] As at November 2026, the Hawaii State Department of Health Vital Records page "Marriage and Civil Union Licenses" (read live 16 November 2026): all marriage performers (officiants or solemnisers) must be licensed by the State of Hawaii Department of Health (section 572-12, Hawaii Revised Statutes) before performing a marriage or civil union; performers register online at https://marriage.ehawaii.gov.

As at November 2026, Cook Islands Ministry of Justice 'Marriage License' page (read live 26 November 2026; page metadata modified 17 October 2022), which describes obtaining a licence 'pursuant to the Marriage Act 1973': 'A legal marriage in the Cook Islands requires a marriage license. Persons being married must be at least 16 years old and those who are under the age of 21 years old require parental consent to be married.'

As at November 2026, Cook Islands Ministry of Justice 'Marriage License' (read live 26 November 2026): 'An Officiating Minister or Marriage Celebrant registered with the Ministry of Justice must be selected to solemnise a marriage. Alternatively, the Registrar of Marriages can be requested to solemnise the marriage at the Ministry of Justice.'

As at November 2026, Cook Islands Ministry of Justice 'Marriage License' (read live 26 November 2026): 'Both persons to be married must give Notice of their intended marriage by appearing at the Ministry of Justice and making a statutory declaration in the prescribed form.' 'Both persons must provide copies of their birth certificates, passports, and, where relevant, divorce decrees or death certificates of deceased spouses.'

As at November 2026, Cook Islands Ministry of Justice 'Marriage License' (read live 26 November 2026): 'A marriage license may only be issued by the Registrar of Marriages three days after the Notice is given unless a Waiver is sought and granted.' 'A marriage license describes the place of marriage and will expire after three months if the marriage is not solemnised.' 'A marriage must be solemnised at the place described in the marriage license'. After the ceremony the Marriage Register form 'must be signed by the bride, bridegroom, two witnesses, and the person who solemnised the marriage' and delivered to the Ministry of Justice. (The page lists fees; none are recorded here.)

As at November 2026, Cook Islands Ministry of Justice 'Marriage License' (read live 26 November 2026), verbatim and for quotation only: 'Presently, the Marriage Act 1973 prohibits any marriage between close family members (e.g. brother and sister; grandmother and grandson) or two persons of the same gender.' This is the Ministry's description of the Act, not the Act's own text; if used at all, quote it exactly with no added position.

As at November 2026, Samoa Bureau of Statistics, 'Births, Deaths & Marriages - Frequently Asked Questions' (read live 26 November 2026): the BDM Division 'registers all births, deaths, marriages' in Samoa and issues 'official certificates for use in Samoa and overseas'. To register a marriage: 'Submission of a Marriage Register from a licensed marriage officer (minister, registrar, or appointed marriage celebrant).' 'Marriages must be registered within 14 days of the ceremony.' The page does not describe notice, licence or document steps for visiting couples. (The page lists fees; none are recorded here.)

As at November 2026, Australian Consulate-General Papeete, 'Mariages en Polynésie française' (French-language page, read live 26 November 2026; the English URL /fppa/marriage.html returned 404). Translated: the Consulate cannot advise on requirements for Australians marrying abroad; in French Polynesia 'les mairies des communes concernées' (the relevant town halls) can advise on requirements, including documents, and confirm applicants' eligibility. Local authorities may ask for a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI) or Certificat de Célibat and a Certificat de Coutume, and French authorities may ask that foreign documents be apostilled in the country that issued them. The Consulate-General does not issue CNIs; it can provide a letter meeting the criteria of a Certificat de Coutume only once you have obtained a CNI.

insider_details.detail: Every tropical entry except New Caledonia shares the same November to April cyclone season on Smartraveller, and New Caledonia runs to May; for a wedding in those months, book a covered ceremony option and give guests a buffer day either side, because Smartraveller says flights can be delayed or suspended and available flights fill quickly.

In Tonga, Sabbath laws limit loud music on Sundays and airports and tours do not run, and in Samoa Sunday activities are extremely limited; avoid a Saturday-night wedding that spills into Sunday or a Sunday departure day, and confirm the venue's Sunday rules early.

In the Cook Islands the licence names the place of marriage and the ceremony must happen there, and both of you must appear at the Ministry of Justice to give notice at least three days before (unless a waiver is granted); plan to land several working days before the wedding and settle the exact site, including any wet-weather site, before you give notice.

New Zealand works the same way: the ceremony can only take place at the places on the licence application, so name a back-up venue, and couples from outside New Zealand must visit a registry office on arrival to sign a declaration before the wedding.

For Tahiti, the Australian Consulate-General in Papeete cannot issue a CNI or notarise documents, and French authorities may ask for apostilled Australian documents; get the CNI and any apostilles in Australia before you fly, then ask the Consulate for the Certificat de Coutume letter.

New Caledonia carries a higher Smartraveller level than its neighbours, and authorities may impose curfews and alcohol-sale bans at short notice; avoid dates around 13 May and 24 September, and make sure contracts cover a curfew or a suspended flight.
